ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the rhombus OABC has its side OA on the positive half of the $x$-axis, and the graph of the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{k}{x}(x>0)$ passes through the midpoint $D$ of the diagonal OB and the vertex $C$. If the area of the rhombus OABC is 12, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the coordinates of point A be $(a, 0)$, and the coordinates of point C be $\left(c, \frac{k}{c}\right)$, \\
$\because$ the area of the rhombus is 12, \\
$\therefore a \cdot \frac{k}{c}=12$, \\
$\because$ D is the midpoint of the diagonal OB, \\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point D are: $\left(\frac{a+c}{2}, \frac{k}{2c}\right)$, \\
$\therefore \frac{a+c}{2} \cdot \frac{k}{2c}=k$, \\
thus $a=3c$, \\
$\therefore 3c \cdot \frac{k}{c}=12$, \\
solving this gives $k=\boxed{4}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the rhombus OABC has its side OA on the positive half of the $x$-axis, and the graph of the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{k}{x}(x>0)$ passes through the midpoint $D$ of the diagonal OB and the vertex C. If the area of the rhombus OABC is 12, what is the value of $k$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the coordinates of point A be $(a, 0)$, and the coordinates of point C be $\left(c, \frac{k}{c}\right)$, \\ 
$\because$ the area of the rhombus is 12, \\ 
$\therefore a \cdot \frac{k}{c}=12$, \\ 
$\because$ D is the midpoint of the diagonal OB, \\ 
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point D are: $\left(\frac{a+c}{2}, \frac{k}{2c}\right)$, \\ 
$\therefore \frac{a+c}{2} \cdot \frac{k}{2c}=k$, \\ 
thus $a=3c$, \\ 
$\therefore 3c \cdot \frac{k}{c}=12$, \\ 
solving this gives $k=\boxed{4}$
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA is located on the positive half of the x-axis; quadrilateral OABC is a rhombus inclined toward the upper right, C is in the first quadrant and located to the upper right of O, B is the upper-right vertex; OB is a diagonal, D is marked on OB; the inverse proportional function curve y=k/x is located in the first quadrant, and passes through point C and point D.

Then reason: Let A=(a,0). Because C is on the curve y=k/x, let C=(c,k/c). A rhombus is also a parallelogram, so B=A+C=(a+c,k/c). D is the midpoint of OB, therefore D=((a+c)/2,k/(2c)). Also because D is also on y=k/x, so x_D y_D=k, that is ((a+c)/2)·(k/(2c))=k. Since k>0, it can be simplified to a+c=4c, so a=3c. The area of the rhombus can be found by the base OA multiplied by the corresponding height, the base length is a, the height is k/c, therefore a·(k/c)=12. Substituting a=3c, get 3c·(k/c)=12, that is 3k=12, so k=4.
